Algorithm implementation: src/railway_delay/platforming.py. It creates a candidate priority-weighted interval plan and uses a minimum-wait FCFS safeguard when that candidate increases total wait.
These are simplified software checks, not an operational railway safety case.
SimPy is a process-based discrete-event simulation framework with limited-capacity shared resources: https://simpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/simpy_intro/shared_resources.html

text: Synthetic scenarios generated with fixed seeds. The 36-movement case uses 6 platforms, moderate demand, seed 42. The 60-movement case uses 4 platforms, busy demand, seed 7.
Randomized ranges are explicit scenario assumptions, not empirical railway failure distributions.

10,000 runs, seed 2068. Static conflict risk means nominal platform reservations overlap after perturbation. Zero post-queue resource collisions are guaranteed by the exclusive resource model and are not a safety certification.
